/* ls_tramp_asm.c --- the validated trampoline_x86_64.S, wrapped in a file-scope
   asm block because the TMM filelist compiles C only.

   GENERATED from trampoline_x86_64.S by `make tramp-asm`. Do not hand-edit: on
   2026-08-17 Phase 3 was applied to THIS file and not to the .S, so the two
   disagreed and the next regeneration would have silently reverted the change.
   check-tramp-mirror fails the build if they drift. */
#if defined(__x86_64__)
__asm__(
"/*\n"
" * trampoline_x86_64.S --- the patched-entry trampoline, System V AMD64.\n"
" *\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *  WHY THIS EXISTS, given that the VM already works without it\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *\n"
" * The integration built on 2026-08-12 uses a DESIGNED-IN call site: 39 lines of\n"
" * C added to http_psm.c, where the compiler owns the calling convention and the\n"
" * shim is arch-generic C. That works, and it needs none of this file.\n"
" *\n"
" * This is for the other claim --- attaching to a function NOBODY EDITED. There\n"
" * the compiler reserved a few bytes at the entry and arming rewrites them into a\n"
" * CALL to here. There is no C frame to borrow, so everything the ABI says a\n"
" * caller may rely on has to be preserved by hand. That is the whole content of\n"
" * this file, and it is why development-scope.md calls item 1 badly understated\n"
" * at \"a page of asm per arch\": the assembly is short, the ABI edge cases are not.\n"
" *\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *  MEASURED FACTS ABOUT THE TARGET --- not assumptions\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *\n"
" * From the BNK build of tmm/tmm at e2104734a9, x86-64\n"
" * (tmm64.no_pgo, build-id verified against its own debug file):\n"
" *\n"
" *   1. IBT IS ON.  403 of 500 sampled functions begin with `endbr64`\n"
" *      (f3 0f 1e fa).  Any indirect branch to a location without an endbranch\n"
" *      faults on CET hardware, so THIS TRAMPOLINE MUST START WITH ONE, and the\n"
" *      patch must not destroy the target's own.\n"
" *\n"
" *   2. THE PAD SITS AFTER endbr64.  With -fpatchable-function-entry=5,0 the\n"
" *      nops are emitted after the entry label, and with IBT they land after the\n"
" *      endbranch:  f3 0f 1e fa  90 90 90 90 90\n"
" *      That is why FIVE is the right pad: `call rel32` is exactly 5 bytes\n"
" *      (e8 xx xx xx xx), so arming replaces the nops in place and DISPLACES NO\n"
" *      REAL INSTRUCTION.  Nothing has to be relocated or re-executed --- which\n"
" *      removes the single largest source of complexity in this kind of hook.\n"
" *\n"
" *      IT MUST BE `call`, NOT `jmp`, and an earlier draft of this file said\n"
" *      jmp.  A jmp pushes nothing, so the `ret` on the fall-through path below\n"
" *      would return to the hooked function's CALLER --- i.e. it would silently\n"
" *      behave as a safe return, always, and the body would never run.  `call`\n"
" *      pushes the address of the instruction after the patch, which IS the\n"
" *      body, so `ret` continues into it.  Verified on hardware, not reasoned:\n"
" *      see check-tramp, which patches a stand-in function and asserts that the\n"
" *      body runs on fall-through and does not on safe return.\n"
" *\n"
" *   3. ARGUMENTS MOVE IMMEDIATELY.  A real target begins\n"
" *          mov %rcx,%r12 ; push %rbp ; mov %rdx,%rbp ; push %rbx ; sub $0x28,%rsp\n"
" *      so the argument registers are consumed within the first few instructions.\n"
" *      The trampoline therefore runs BEFORE the prologue and must capture them\n"
" *      first; there is no later point at which rdi/rsi/rdx/rcx still hold the\n"
" *      arguments.\n"
" *\n"
" *   4. .eh_frame IS PRESENT.  A core dump taken while a shield is running must\n"
" *      still unwind, so this file carries CFI directives.  Without them the\n"
" *      backtrace stops here, and \"the crash we were shielding is now\n"
" *      undebuggable\" is not an acceptable trade.\n"
" *\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *  WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT DO\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *\n"
" *   - It does not save FP/SIMD state.  See the note at ls_tramp_save_fp below:\n"
" *     that is a real decision, not an omission, and it is wrong for any hook\n"
" *     whose shield might touch floating point.\n"
" *   - It does not handle varargs (%rax as the vector-register count).\n"
" *   - It does not implement the safe-return path's value selection --- the host\n"
" *     decides what a safe return means per hook (development-scope.md item 7);\n"
" *     this returns the value the hook slot carries.\n"
" *   - It is NOT re-entrant.  ls_vm.c hands every invocation the same per-instance\n"
" *     program stack, which is safe only because TMM is run-to-completion and two\n"
" *     invocations never overlap on a core.  A shield that re-entered its own\n"
" *     hooked path would corrupt that stack.  Guarding it is on item 1's list.\n"
" *   - It is not wired to anything.  Arming (item 2) writes the jump; nothing here\n"
" *     writes code.\n"
" *\n"
" * Status: candidate artifact.  It assembles.  Nothing calls it.\n"
" */\n"
"\n"
"/* ===================================================================\n"
" *  ONE TRAMPOLINE PER SLOT --- why this is a macro\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *\n"
" * There used to be ONE trampoline whose slot arrived as a patched immediate\n"
" * (ls_tramp_slot_insn). That meant the slot was global: arming a second hook with a\n"
" * different slot rewrote the immediate for every hook already armed, silently\n"
" * re-pointing all of them at the new slot's ctx builder and program.\n"
" *\n"
" * On 2026-08-17 four reset functions were armed with slots 5, 6, 3, 3. The immediate\n"
" * ended at 3, so rst_why dispatched through the rst_why_preserve builder, which reads\n"
" * the cause from a4 rather than a5 --- a4 is `reason`, which is 0 --- and every record\n"
" * came back with an empty cause. Nothing failed and nothing logged.\n"
" *\n"
" * The header above already said the design assumed \"one trampoline per armed hook, so\n"
" * the slot is known when the trampoline is created\". This makes that true.\n"
" *\n"
" * WHY STATIC COPIES RATHER THAN ALLOCATED ONES. Copying a trampoline into mmap'd\n"
" * memory needs PROT_EXEC, needs to land within +/-2GB of .text for `call rel32` (see\n"
" * REACH above), and needs the internal `call ls_tramp_dispatch` relocated by hand\n"
" * because a copied rel32 points at the wrong place. Emitting one per slot at assembly\n"
" * time has none of those problems: each copy's dispatch call is assembled correctly,\n"
" * every copy is in .text so reach is guaranteed, and the slot is an immediate the\n"
" * assembler wrote. The cost is ~70 bytes of .text per slot.\n"
" *\n"
" * The slot is now ASSEMBLED IN, so nothing patches it and there is no shared mutable\n"
" * state left for a second arm to corrupt.\n"
" */\n"
"    .text\n"
"    .macro LS_TRAMP n\n"
"    .globl  ls_trampoline_slot\\n\n"
"    .type   ls_trampoline_slot\\n, @function\n"
"\n"
"/*\n"
" * Reached by the 5-byte `call rel32` written over the patch nops.  On entry the\n"
" * stack and registers are exactly as the hooked function's caller left them,\n"
" * except that the call has pushed the address of the instruction AFTER the\n"
" * patch --- i.e. the hooked function's real body.\n"
" *\n"
" * REACH: `call rel32` spans +/-2GB from the patch site.  TMM's .text is ~30MB,\n"
" * so a trampoline living in .text is always in range.  A trampoline in\n"
" * mmap'd memory is NOT guaranteed to be, and five bytes cannot hold an indirect\n"
" * call --- so either the trampoline is linked into the image, or arming must\n"
" * allocate its trampolines within +/-2GB of .text and fail closed when it\n"
" * cannot.  That constraint belongs to item 2 and is easy to miss until a large\n"
" * ASLR offset makes it intermittent.\n"
" */\n"
"ls_trampoline_slot\\n:\n"
"    .cfi_startproc\n"
"    endbr64                         /* fact 1: IBT. Without this, the indirect\n"
"                                     * branch faults on CET hardware. */\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Fact 3: capture the argument registers before anything else can clobber\n"
"     * them.  System V AMD64 integer arguments, in order:\n"
"     *     rdi rsi rdx rcx r8 r9\n"
"     * rax additionally carries the vector-register count for varargs calls,\n"
"     * which this file does not support --- see the header.\n"
"     */\n"
"    pushq   %rdi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rsi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rdx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rcx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %r8\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %r9\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rax\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Caller-saved registers the shield path may clobber.  r10 and r11 are\n"
"     * scratch under the ABI, so the hooked function cannot rely on them --- but\n"
"     * WE are running before the hooked function, on behalf of its caller, and\n"
"     * the caller cannot rely on them either.  Saved anyway: the cost is two\n"
"     * pushes, and the failure mode if this reasoning is ever wrong is a\n"
"     * miscompile-class bug that would take days to find.\n"
"     */\n"
"    pushq   %r10\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %r11\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Align to 16 before the call.  Nine pushes above (72 bytes) plus the 8-byte\n"
"     * return address leaves rsp ≡ 0 (mod 16) already, but the alignment is\n"
"     * asserted rather than assumed, because getting it wrong shows up only when\n"
"     * the callee happens to use an aligned SSE move.\n"
"     */\n"
"    subq    $8, %rsp\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * ls_tramp_dispatch(slot, regs) --- plain C, in ls_tramp.c.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * The ctx build lives in C on purpose.  It is per-hook, generated from the\n"
"     * build's DWARF (item 6), and changes whenever a hook's signature does;\n"
"     * putting it in assembly would mean regenerating assembly per hook, which is\n"
"     * the thing this design is trying to avoid.  The assembly is generic; only\n"
"     * the C is per-hook.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * THE SLOT INDEX IS A PATCHED IMMEDIATE, not a register.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * An earlier draft of this file said the slot \"arrives in r11\".  That is\n"
"     * wrong: at hook entry r11 holds whatever the hooked function's CALLER left\n"
"     * there.  Nothing has put a slot index in it, and reading it would feed the\n"
"     * dispatcher garbage.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * This is one trampoline per armed hook, so the slot is known when the\n"
"     * trampoline is created.  `movl $imm32` puts it in the instruction stream;\n"
"     * arming (item 2) writes the four bytes at ls_tramp_slot_imm.  A single\n"
"     * SHARED trampoline is the alternative and would have to recover the slot\n"
"     * from the return address --- possible, slower, and a trade that belongs to\n"
"     * item 2 rather than here.\n"
"     */\n"
"    movl    $\\n, %edi              /* slot: ASSEMBLED IN, never patched */\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * The label sits on the INSTRUCTION, not on the immediate.  An earlier draft\n"
"     * used `ls_tramp_slot_imm = . + 1` to point straight at the four bytes;\n"
"     * the code was correct, but a symbol in the middle of an instruction makes\n"
"     * objdump restart disassembly there and render everything after it as\n"
"     * garbage --- in the one file whose whole audience is someone reading a\n"
"     * disassembler.  Arming adds the +1 itself; that is one line in item 2\n"
"     * against permanently unreadable output here.\n"
"     */\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Stack layout at this point, from rsp upward.  Nine pushes (72 bytes) then\n"
"     * `sub $8`, so the saved registers begin at 8(%rsp):\n"
"     *\n"
"     *    0  alignment gap      40  r8\n"
"     *    8  r11                48  rcx\n"
"     *   16  r10                56  rdx\n"
"     *   24  rax                64  rsi\n"
"     *   32  r9                 72  rdi   <- the hooked function's arg0\n"
"     *   80  return address (into the hooked function's body)\n"
"     *\n"
"     * An earlier draft had every one of these eight bytes low --- it read rsi as\n"
"     * rdi, rdx as rsi, and so on.  That does not crash; it silently hands the\n"
"     * shield the wrong arguments, which is the worst way for this to be wrong.\n"
"     */\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * ONE leaq, NOT five movq --- this is Phase 3.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * The five movq that were here loaded arg0..arg4 into the ABI argument\n"
"     * registers, forwarding exactly FIVE arguments because rdi carries the slot.\n"
"     * A sixth would have landed on the stack, and rst_cause --- the human-written\n"
"     * reason string, and at flow_table.c a lookup into an ENUMERATED cause table\n"
"     * --- is the sixth. It was simply dropped.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * Passing the ADDRESS of the saved block hands the C side all nine saved\n"
"     * registers, so no future hook signature touches this file again. It is also\n"
"     * strictly less work than the five loads it replaces.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * 8(%rsp) is r11, the LOWEST saved register --- struct ls_regs in ls_arm.h has\n"
"     * its fields in exactly this order. 0(%rsp) is the alignment gap and must NOT\n"
"     * be included: pointing there shifts every field by eight and hands the shield\n"
"     * arg1 where it expects arg0, silently. An earlier draft of this file made\n"
"     * exactly that off-by-eight mistake with the movq forms.\n"
"     */\n"
"    leaq    8(%rsp), %rsi           /* -> struct ls_regs, r11 first            */\n"
"    movq    80(%rsp), %rdx          /* patched site's continuation address    */\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Returns a {int verdict; uint64_t safe_value} pair, which System V returns\n"
"     * in rax:rdx --- exactly the registers the code below reads.  An earlier\n"
"     * draft passed a seventh `safe_out` POINTER argument, which the ABI would\n"
"     * have placed on the stack while this call site passed only six registers:\n"
"     * the callee would have dereferenced whatever happened to be there.\n"
"     */\n"
"    call    ls_tramp_dispatch_at    /* -> eax: 0 fall through, 1 safe return   */\n"
"                                    /*    rdx: the declared safe value          */\n"
"\n"
"    addq    $8, %rsp\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"\n"
"    testl   %eax, %eax\n"
"    jnz     1f                      /* numeric local: reusable per expansion */\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Fall through: restore everything and continue into the hooked function's\n"
"     * real body.  Fact 2 is what makes this trivial --- the patch overwrote only\n"
"     * nops, so the body is intact and the return address already points at it.\n"
"     * `ret` therefore lands exactly where execution would have gone had nothing\n"
"     * been armed.\n"
"     */\n"
"    popq    %r11\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r10\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rax\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r9\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r8\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rcx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rdx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rsi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rdi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    ret\n"
"\n"
"1:\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Safe return: the hooked function's body must NOT run.  Discard the saved\n"
"     * registers, drop the return address that points into the body, and return\n"
"     * to the hooked function's own caller with the declared safe value.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * ls_tramp_dispatch leaves that value in rdx --- chosen because rax already\n"
"     * carries the verdict.  What counts as safe is per-hook and belongs to the\n"
"     * safe-return policy table (item 7); this file only delivers it.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * THE LIMIT WORTH STATING: this is correct only for a return type that fits\n"
"     * in rax.  A struct returned by hidden pointer, or anything using rdx:rax or\n"
"     * the x87/SSE return registers, needs its own path.  Item 7 restricts v1 to\n"
"     * trivial returns for exactly this reason, and this file enforces nothing ---\n"
"     * admitting a shield on a hook with a non-trivial return type is an\n"
"     * admission-time error, not a runtime one.\n"
"     */\n"
"    addq    $72, %rsp               /* discard the nine saved registers        */\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -72\n"
"    movq    %rdx, %rax              /* the declared safe value                 */\n"
"    addq    $8, %rsp                /* drop the return-into-body address       */\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    ret                             /* -> the hooked function's caller         */\n"
"\n"
"    .cfi_endproc\n"
"    .size   ls_trampoline_slot\\n, .-ls_trampoline_slot\\n\n"
"    .endm\n"
"\n"
"/* One per slot in ls_slots.h (0..7). Adding a slot there means adding an expansion\n"
" * here AND extending the table below --- the _Static_asserts in ls_slots.h cannot see\n"
" * this file, so ls_arm.c range-checks the index against LS_TRAMP_SLOTS instead. */\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 0\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 1\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 2\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 3\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 4\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 5\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 6\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 7\n"
"/* Slots 8-11 added 2026-08-18 for the ssl__err tracepoint (slot 8) plus headroom.\n"
" * Expanding is cheap --- each slot is ~40 bytes of .text whose only per-slot content\n"

" */\n"

"    .globl  ls_fexit_slot\\n\n"
"    .type   ls_fexit_slot\\n, @function\n"
"ls_fexit_slot\\n:\n"
"    .cfi_startproc\n"
"    endbr64\n"
"    pushq   %r9\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %r8\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rcx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rdx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rsi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rdi\n"

"    leaq    0(%rsp),  %rdx           /* arg2: const uint64_t *args (rdi..r9)  */\n"
"    call    ls_fexit_enter\n"
"    popq    %rdi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rsi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rdx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rcx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r8\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r9\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    ret                             /* -> body-return, into the hooked fn body */\n"
"    .cfi_endproc\n"
"    .size   ls_fexit_slot\\n, .-ls_fexit_slot\\n\n"
"    .endm\n"
"\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 0\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 1\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 2\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 3\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 4\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 5\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 6\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 7\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 8\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 9\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 10\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 11\n"

"/* The shared stub every exit slot installs. Reached by the body's `ret`:\n"

"    .type   ls_fexit_stub, @function\n"

"    .cfi_startproc\n"
"    pushq   %rax                    /* save return value (low)                */\n"
"    pushq   %rdx                    /* save return value (high)               */\n"

"    popq    %rdx\n"
"    popq    %rax\n"
"    pushq   %r11\n"
"    ret                             /* -> real caller, rax:rdx intact          */\n"
"    .cfi_endproc\n"
"    .size   ls_fexit_stub, .-ls_fexit_stub\n"
"\n"

"    .section .rodata\n"
"    .globl  ls_fexit_table\n"
"    .type   ls_fexit_table, @object\n"
"    .align  8\n"
"ls_fexit_table:\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot0\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot1\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot2\n"

"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot4\n"

"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot6\n"

"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot8\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot9\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot10\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot11\n"

"    .globl  ls_fexit_slot_count\n"

"     * ONE leaq, NOT five movq --- this is Phase 3.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * The five movq that were here loaded arg0..arg4 into the ABI argument\n"
"     * registers, forwarding exactly FIVE arguments because rdi carries the slot.\n"
"     * A sixth would have landed on the stack, and rst_cause --- the human-written\n"
"     * reason string, and at flow_table.c a lookup into an ENUMERATED cause table\n"
"     * --- is the sixth. It was simply dropped.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * Passing the ADDRESS of the saved block hands the C side all nine saved\n"
"     * registers, so no future hook signature touches this file again. It is also\n"
"     * strictly less work than the five loads it replaces.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * 8(%rsp) is r11, the LOWEST saved register --- struct ls_regs in ls_arm.h has\n"
"     * its fields in exactly this order. 0(%rsp) is the alignment gap and must NOT\n"
"     * be included: pointing there shifts every field by eight and hands the shield\n"
"     * arg1 where it expects arg0, silently. An earlier draft of this file made\n"
"     * exactly that off-by-eight mistake with the movq forms.\n"
"     */\n"
"    leaq    8(%rsp), %rsi           /* -> struct ls_regs, r11 first            */\n"
"    movq    80(%rsp), %rdx          /* patched site's continuation address    */\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Returns a {int verdict; uint64_t safe_value} pair, which System V returns\n"
"     * in rax:rdx --- exactly the registers the code below reads.  An earlier\n"
"     * draft passed a seventh `safe_out` POINTER argument, which the ABI would\n"
"     * have placed on the stack while this call site passed only six registers:\n"
"     * the callee would have dereferenced whatever happened to be there.\n"
"     */\n"
"    call    ls_tramp_dispatch_at    /* -> eax: 0 fall through, 1 safe return   */\n"
"                                    /*    rdx: the declared safe value          */\n"
"\n"
"    addq    $8, %rsp\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"\n"
"    testl   %eax, %eax\n"
"    jnz     1f                      /* numeric local: reusable per expansion */\n"
"\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Fall through: restore everything and continue into the hooked function's\n"
"     * real body.  Fact 2 is what makes this trivial --- the patch overwrote only\n"
"     * nops, so the body is intact and the return address already points at it.\n"
"     * `ret` therefore lands exactly where execution would have gone had nothing\n"
"     * been armed.\n"
"     */\n"
"    popq    %r11\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r10\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rax\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r9\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r8\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rcx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rdx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rsi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rdi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    ret\n"
"\n"
"1:\n"
"    /*\n"
"     * Safe return: the hooked function's body must NOT run.  Discard the saved\n"
"     * registers, drop the return address that points into the body, and return\n"
"     * to the hooked function's own caller with the declared safe value.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * ls_tramp_dispatch leaves that value in rdx --- chosen because rax already\n"
"     * carries the verdict.  What counts as safe is per-hook and belongs to the\n"
"     * safe-return policy table (item 7); this file only delivers it.\n"
"     *\n"
"     * THE LIMIT WORTH STATING: this is correct only for a return type that fits\n"
"     * in rax.  A struct returned by hidden pointer, or anything using rdx:rax or\n"
"     * the x87/SSE return registers, needs its own path.  Item 7 restricts v1 to\n"
"     * trivial returns for exactly this reason, and this file enforces nothing ---\n"
"     * admitting a shield on a hook with a non-trivial return type is an\n"
"     * admission-time error, not a runtime one.\n"
"     */\n"
"    addq    $72, %rsp               /* discard the nine saved registers        */\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -72\n"
"    movq    %rdx, %rax              /* the declared safe value                 */\n"
"    addq    $8, %rsp                /* drop the return-into-body address       */\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    ret                             /* -> the hooked function's caller         */\n"
"\n"
"    .cfi_endproc\n"
"    .size   ls_trampoline_slot\\n, .-ls_trampoline_slot\\n\n"
"    .endm\n"
"\n"
"/* One per slot in ls_slots.h (0..7). Adding a slot there means adding an expansion\n"
" * here AND extending the table below --- the _Static_asserts in ls_slots.h cannot see\n"
" * this file, so ls_arm.c range-checks the index against LS_TRAMP_SLOTS instead. */\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 0\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 1\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 2\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 3\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 4\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 5\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 6\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 7\n"
"/* Slots 8-11 added 2026-08-18 for the ssl__err tracepoint (slot 8) plus headroom.\n"
" * Expanding is cheap --- each slot is ~40 bytes of .text whose only per-slot content\n"
" * is the immediate --- and running out is not, because a hook forced to share a slot\n"
" * with a different ctx shape is exactly the 2026-08-17 empty-cause bug. */\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 8\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 9\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 10\n"
"    LS_TRAMP 11\n"
"\n"
"/* Kept as an alias so anything still referencing the old single entry point links,\n"
" * and so a reader grepping for it finds this note rather than nothing. Slot 0 is the\n"
" * shield slot; using this symbol for a hook of any other shape is the bug above. */\n"
"    .globl  ls_trampoline_entry\n"
"    .set    ls_trampoline_entry, ls_trampoline_slot0\n"
"\n"
"/* Address table, so C indexes by slot instead of hard-coding twelve symbol names.\n"
" * .rodata: nothing writes it at run time, and a trampoline table in writable memory\n"
" * would be a control-flow target sitting in mutable storage. */\n"
"    .section .rodata\n"
"    .globl  ls_trampoline_table\n"
"    .type   ls_trampoline_table, @object\n"
"    .align  8\n"
"ls_trampoline_table:\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot0\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot1\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot2\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot3\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot4\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot5\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot6\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot7\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot8\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot9\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot10\n"
"    .quad   ls_trampoline_slot11\n"
"    .size   ls_trampoline_table, .-ls_trampoline_table\n"
"\n"
"/*\n"
" * HOW MANY SLOTS THIS FILE ACTUALLY BUILT, exported so C can check rather than trust.\n"
" *\n"
" * The count lived in THREE places that had to agree by hand: the expansions above,\n"
" * LS_TRAMP_SLOTS in ls_arm.c, and LS_MAX_SLOTS in ls_vm.c. Nothing compared them. If a\n"
" * C-side constant were ever the larger, `ls_trampoline_table[slot]` would read past the\n"
" * end of a .rodata array and arm a hook at whatever address followed --- a wild jump\n"
" * target written into live .text, which is the worst failure this codebase can have.\n"
" *\n"
" * An extern array of unspecified size cannot be size-checked by the linker, so the\n"
" * count is published as data and verified at run time by ls_arm.c.\n"
" */\n"
"    .globl  ls_trampoline_slot_count\n"
"    .type   ls_trampoline_slot_count, @object\n"
"    .align  8\n"
"ls_trampoline_slot_count:\n"
"    .quad   12\n"
"    .size   ls_trampoline_slot_count, .-ls_trampoline_slot_count\n"
"    .text\n"
"\n"
"/*\n"
" * FP/SIMD, deliberately absent.\n"
" *\n"
" * Saving xmm0-15 costs ~256 bytes of stack and 16 stores/loads per invocation,\n"
" * on a path whose whole budget is ~26 cycles (the measured JIT floor).  It would\n"
" * dominate.  It is omitted here because uBPF's generated code does not touch\n"
" * SSE --- but that is a property of TODAY'S uBPF, not a guarantee, and it does\n"
" * not hold if a helper is ever added that does.\n"
" *\n"
" * So this is a bet, and it should be an explicit one: either the admission\n"
" * pipeline proves the program touches no FP state, or the trampoline pays for\n"
" * it.  Choosing silently is how a rare, data-dependent corruption gets shipped.\n"
" */\n"
"/* ===================================================================\n"
" *  THE FUNCTION-EXIT TRAMPOLINE --- one per slot, plus a shared stub\n"
" * ===================================================================\n"
" *\n"
" * Arming an EXIT hook patches the SAME entry pad (same `call rel32`, same\n"
" * ls_arm), but points it at ls_fexit_slot<n> instead of ls_trampoline_slot<n>.\n"
" * There is no pad at a function's exit --- a `ret` is one byte --- so exit is\n"
" * done by HIJACKING THE RETURN ADDRESS, the way kretprobes/frida/bpftime do it.\n"
" *\n"
" * On entry (reached by the pad's `call`):\n"
" *     [rsp]    = body-return    (into the hooked fn body)\n"
" *     [rsp+8]  = caller-return   <-- the slot ls_fexit_enter overwrites\n"
" * ls_fexit_enter records {slot address, real caller-return, args, THIS slot} on\n"
" * the shadow stack (ls_fexit.c) and writes &ls_fexit_stub over [rsp+8]. We ret\n"
" * into the body; the body's own `ret` then lands in the stub, which reads the\n"
" * return value, pops the matching shadow frame (reclaiming any a non-local exit\n"
" * skipped), and returns to the real caller. Proven in check_fexit.c.\n"
" *\n"
" * The slot is ASSEMBLED IN (movl $n), exactly as the entry trampoline does it,\n"
" * so a second arm cannot corrupt a shared immediate (the 2026-08-17 bug).\n"
" * IBT: this is a `call` target, so endbr64; the STUB is a `ret` target and needs\n"
" * none, and must return via `push;ret` (a post-call address has no endbranch).\n"
" */\n"
"    .macro LS_FEXIT n\n"
"    .globl  ls_fexit_slot\\n\n"
"    .type   ls_fexit_slot\\n, @function\n"
"ls_fexit_slot\\n:\n"
"    .cfi_startproc\n"
"    endbr64\n"
"    pushq   %r9\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %r8\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rcx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rdx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rsi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    pushq   %rdi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset 8\n"
"    /* [rsp+0..40] = rdi,rsi,rdx,rcx,r8,r9 ; [rsp+48]=body-return ;\n"
"     * [rsp+56]=caller-return. rsp%16==0 (entry 0, +48). */\n"
"    movl    $\\n, %edi                /* arg0: slot (assembled in)             */\n"
"    leaq    56(%rsp), %rsi           /* arg1: uint64_t *slot (caller-ret addr)*/\n"
"    leaq    0(%rsp),  %rdx           /* arg2: const uint64_t *args (rdi..r9)  */\n"
"    call    ls_fexit_enter\n"
"    popq    %rdi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rsi\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rdx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %rcx\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r8\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    popq    %r9\n"
"    .cfi_adjust_cfa_offset -8\n"
"    ret                             /* -> body-return, into the hooked fn body */\n"
"    .cfi_endproc\n"
"    .size   ls_fexit_slot\\n, .-ls_fexit_slot\\n\n"
"    .endm\n"
"\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 0\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 1\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 2\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 3\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 4\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 5\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 6\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 7\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 8\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 9\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 10\n"
"    LS_FEXIT 11\n"
"\n"
"/* Alias so a stand-in armed at slot 0 (and anything grepping for it) resolves,\n"
" * mirroring ls_trampoline_entry. */\n"
"    .globl  ls_fexit_entry\n"
"    .set    ls_fexit_entry, ls_fexit_slot0\n"
"\n"
"/* The shared stub every exit slot installs. Reached by the body's `ret`:\n"
" *     rax(:rdx) = return value ; rsp = (hijacked slot)+8 ; rsp%16==0.\n"
" * Preserve the return value across the C call; return to the real caller via\n"
" * push;ret (IBT-safe). Punts on FP return registers, like the entry path. */\n"
"    .globl  ls_fexit_stub\n"
"    .type   ls_fexit_stub, @function\n"
"ls_fexit_stub:\n"
"    .cfi_startproc\n"
"    pushq   %rax                    /* save return value (low)                */\n"
"    pushq   %rdx                    /* save return value (high)               */\n"
"    leaq    16(%rsp), %rdi          /* arg0: cur = SP just after the body ret  */\n"
"    movq    8(%rsp),  %rsi          /* arg1: retval                            */\n"
"    call    ls_fexit_leave          /* -> real caller-return in rax            */\n"
"    movq    %rax, %r11\n"
"    popq    %rdx\n"
"    popq    %rax\n"
"    pushq   %r11\n"
"    ret                             /* -> real caller, rax:rdx intact          */\n"
"    .cfi_endproc\n"
"    .size   ls_fexit_stub, .-ls_fexit_stub\n"
"\n"
"/* Exit-slot address table + count, mirroring ls_trampoline_table --- so C indexes\n"
" * by slot and can range-check against what this file actually built. */\n"
"    .section .rodata\n"
"    .globl  ls_fexit_table\n"
"    .type   ls_fexit_table, @object\n"
"    .align  8\n"
"ls_fexit_table:\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot0\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot1\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot2\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot3\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot4\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot5\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot6\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot7\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot8\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot9\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot10\n"
"    .quad   ls_fexit_slot11\n"
"    .size   ls_fexit_table, .-ls_fexit_table\n"
"    .globl  ls_fexit_slot_count\n"
"    .type   ls_fexit_slot_count, @object\n"
"    .align  8\n"
"ls_fexit_slot_count:\n"
"    .quad   12\n"
"    .size   ls_fexit_slot_count, .-ls_fexit_slot_count\n"
"    .text\n"
"\n"
"    .section .note.GNU-stack,\"\",@progbits\n"
"\n"
);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Integrate native-qualified program ownership into an existing TMM build tree.

This is an incremental build, not a fresh-tree installer or a live traffic test.
All host paths and the existing toolchain container are explicit inputs.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import time


FILES = (
    "ls_program.h", "ls_program_impl.h", "ls_vm.c", "ls_vm.h",
    "ls_vm_load.c", "ls_map_glue.h", "ls_target.h", "ls_arm.h",
    "ls_tramp.c", "ls_tramp_asm.c",
)
NEW = {"ls_program.h", "ls_program_impl.h"}
WHITELISTS = (
    "src/compile/default_whitelist_x86_64",
    "src/compile/debug_whitelist_x86_64",
)
FUNCTIONS = (
    "ls_program_load", "ls_program_status", "ls_program_mode",
    "ls_program_attach", "ls_program_detach", "ls_program_revoke",
    "ls_program_site_owned", "ls_program_dispatch", "ls_tramp_dispatch_at",
)
TLS = ("g_prog_stack", "g_ls_namespace", "g_ls_map_namespaces")


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    for name in ("source", "tree", "staged", "native", "output"):
        parser.add_argument("--" + name, type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--native-sha256", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--revision", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--container", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--previous", type=Path,
                        help="receipt for an earlier publication into this tree")
    parser.add_argument("--previous-sha256")
    parser.add_argument("--verify-built", action="store_true",
                        help="check a previous successful make without rebuilding")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    for name in ("source", "tree", "staged", "native", "output"):
        setattr(args, name, getattr(args, name).resolve())
    args.output.mkdir()
    base = args.source / "substrate"
    tree = args.tree
    record = dict(passed=False, scope="TMM linked binary only; no package or live test",
                  started=time.time(), commands=[], sources={}, original_sources={})
    record["inputs"] = {key: str(value) for key, value in vars(args).items()}
    record["driver"] = dict(sha256=sha(Path(__file__)), text=Path(__file__).read_text())

    def run(*argv, compact=False):
        argv = list(map(str, argv))
        result = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=tree, capture_output=True, text=True,
                                timeout=120, check=False)
        row = dict(argv=argv, rc=result.returncode, stderr=result.stderr)
        if compact:
            row["stdout_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(result.stdout.encode()).hexdigest()
        else:
            row["stdout"] = result.stdout
        record["commands"].append(row)
        result.check_returncode()
        return result.stdout

    def containers():
        return run("docker", "ps", "-a", "--no-trunc", "--format",
                   "{{.ID}} {{.Names}} {{.Image}}")

    def hashes(paths):
        return {str(path.relative_to(tree)): sha(path) for path in paths}

    with (args.output / "build-result.json").open("x") as receipt:
        try:
            previous = None
            if args.previous:
                assert args.previous_sha256 and sha(args.previous) == args.previous_sha256
                previous = json.loads(args.previous.read_text())
                assert previous["inputs"]["tree"] == str(tree)
                record["previous_sha256"] = sha(args.previous)
            if args.verify_built:
                assert previous and previous.get("returncode") == 0, "no successful make receipt"
            assert sha(args.native) == args.native_sha256, "native receipt hash"
            native = json.loads(args.native.read_text())
            assert native["passed"], "native checks did not pass"
            record["native_sha256"] = sha(args.native)
            record["instructions"] = (tree / "AGENTS.md").read_text()
            record["revision"] = run("git", "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
            assert record["revision"] == args.revision, "TMM revision changed"
            record["status_before"] = run("git", "status", "--porcelain")
            record["containers_before"] = containers()
            inspection = json.loads(run("docker", "inspect", "--format",
                                       "{{json .Mounts}}", args.container))
            assert any(mount["Source"] == str(tree) and mount["Destination"] == "/tmm"
                       for mount in inspection), "container does not mount selected tree"
            record["container_image"] = run("docker", "inspect", "--format",
                                            "{{.Image}}", args.container).strip()
            processes = run("docker", "top", args.container, "-eo", "pid,comm,args")
            for line in processes.splitlines()[1:]:
                fields = line.split()
                assert len(fields) < 2 or fields[1] not in (
                    "make", "gmake", "gcc", "cc1", "cc1plus", "g++", "ld"
                ), "another build is running: " + line
            record["compiler"] = run("docker", "exec", args.container, "gcc", "--version")
            assert "11.4.0" in record["compiler"], "unqualified TMM compiler"
            record["ubpf_revision"] = run("git", "-C", tree / ".ubpf",
                                           "rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
            assert record["ubpf_revision"] == "c900ed9faf1d41358a7ea9217ccd0b64a4ee8d5d"
            record["ubpf_status"] = run("git", "-C", tree / ".ubpf", "status", "--short")

            # The wrapper is generated from the assembly checked by the native suite.
            for name in ("trampoline_x86_64.S", "mk_tramp_asm.py"):
                assert sha(base / name) == native["sources"]["substrate/" + name]["sha256"]
            spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("tramp_generator", base / "mk_tramp_asm.py")
            module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
            spec.loader.exec_module(module)
            assembly = (base / "trampoline_x86_64.S").read_text()
            wrapper = module.PREAMBLE + "".join(module.wrap(line) for line in assembly.split("\n")) + module.EPILOGUE
            assert (base / "ls_tramp_asm.c").read_text() == wrapper, "assembly mirror drift"
            record["assembly_sha256"] = sha(base / "trampoline_x86_64.S")
            record["generated_wrapper_matches_native_assembly"] = True

            protected = [tree / name for name in (
                "src/modules/hudfilter/http2/http2.c",
                "src/modules/hudfilter/ssl/ssl.c", "src/compile/filelist",
                "Makefile.overrides", ".ubpf/build/lib/libubpf.a",
            )]
            protected += [path for path in (tree / "src/base").glob("ls_*.[ch]")
                          if path.name not in FILES]
            protected += [tree / "src/base" / name for name in ("shield_abi.h", "vm_stack_policy.h")]
            record["protected_before"] = hashes(protected)
            if args.verify_built:
                assert record["protected_before"] == previous["protected_before"], "build inputs changed"
            originals = args.output / "originals"
            originals.mkdir()
            # Check all existing substrate dependencies available in the native receipt.
            for path in protected:
                key = "substrate/" + path.name
                if path.parent == tree / "src/base" and path.name != "ls_sig_pubkey.h" and key in native["sources"]:
                    assert sha(path) == native["sources"][key]["sha256"], "unchecked dependency: " + key
            for name in FILES:
                source = base / name
                if name != "ls_tramp_asm.c":
                    assert sha(source) == native["sources"]["substrate/" + name]["sha256"], name
                record["sources"][name] = dict(sha256=sha(source), text=source.read_text())
                target = tree / "src/base" / name
                if previous:
                    assert sha(target) == previous["sources"][name]["sha256"], "tree changed since previous publication: " + name
                    assert sha(target) == sha(args.staged / name), "tree/stage divergence: " + name
                    if args.verify_built:
                        assert sha(source) == sha(target), "new source requires rebuilding: " + name
                    record["original_sources"][name] = dict(sha256=sha(target), text=target.read_text())
                    shutil.copy2(target, originals / name)
                elif name in NEW:

                record["build_command"] = previous["build_command"]

                record["verification_only"] = True

                    shutil.copy2(base / name, tree / "src/base" / name)
                    shutil.copy2(base / name, args.staged / name)
                for name, text in changes.items():
                    (tree / name).write_text(text)

                objects += sorted((tree / "src/compile").glob("obj_x86_64.*/harness.o"))
                record["invalidated_objects"] = list(map(str, objects))
                if objects:
                    run("sudo", "rm", "--", *objects)
                assert all(not path.exists() for path in objects), "stale objects survived"
                record["build_started"] = time.time()
                command = ["script", "-qec", "make tmm", str(args.output / "build.log")]
                record["build_command"] = command
                with (args.output / "console.log").open("xb") as console:
                    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=tree, stdout=console,
                                            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=7200, check=False)
                record["returncode"] = result.returncode
                result.check_returncode()
            record["whitelist_after"] = hashes([tree / name for name in WHITELISTS])

            binary = tree / "src/compile/obj_x86_64.no_pgo/tmm.no_pgo"
            assert binary.stat().st_mtime >= record["build_started"], "stale linked binary"
            symbol_text = run("readelf", "--wide", "--syms", binary, compact=True)
            if args.verify_built:
                old_symbols = next(row for row in previous["commands"]
                                   if row["argv"][:3] == ["readelf", "--wide", "--syms"])
                assert hashlib.sha256(symbol_text.encode()).hexdigest() == old_symbols["stdout_sha256"]
            symbols = {line.split()[-1]: line.split() for line in symbol_text.splitlines()
                       if len(line.split()) >= 8 and line.split()[0].endswith(":")}
            for name in FUNCTIONS:
                assert symbols[name][3] == "FUNC" and symbols[name][6] != "UND", name
            for name in TLS:
                assert symbols[name][3] == "TLS", name
            assert symbols["g_programs"][3] == "OBJECT"
            record["symbols"] = {name: symbols[name] for name in FUNCTIONS + TLS + ("g_programs", "g_slots")}
            record["trampolines"] = {}
            for site in range(12):
                name = "ls_trampoline_slot" + str(site)
                # Slot zero has a public alias. Name-filtered objdump can emit
                # no instructions for that name; use the exact ELF symbol range.
                address = int(symbols[name][1], 16)
                size = int(symbols[name][2])
                assert size > 0 and symbols[name][3] == "FUNC", name
                text = run("objdump", "-d", "--start-address=" + hex(address),
                           "--stop-address=" + hex(address + size), binary)
                assert "<ls_tramp_dispatch_at>" in text and "0x50(%rsp),%rdx" in text, name
                record["trampolines"][name] = text
            run(tree / "bin/diff-globals", binary, tree / WHITELISTS[0])
            record["artifact"] = dict(path=str(binary), sha256=sha(binary),
                                       bytes=binary.stat().st_size, mtime=binary.stat().st_mtime,
                                       notes=run("readelf", "-n", binary))
            shutil.copy2(binary, args.output / "tmm.no_pgo")
            assert sha(args.output / "tmm.no_pgo") == record["artifact"]["sha256"]
            record["protected_after"] = hashes(protected)
            assert record["protected_after"] == record["protected_before"], "protected file changed"
            for name in FILES:
                assert sha(tree / "src/base" / name) == sha(base / name)
                assert sha(args.staged / name) == sha(base / name)
            record["status_after"] = run("git", "status", "--porcelain")
            record["containers_after"] = containers()
            assert record["containers_after"] == record["containers_before"]
            record["passed"] = True
        except BaseException as error:
            record["error"] = repr(error)
            raise
        finally:
            record["finished"] = time.time()
            for name in ("build.log", "console.log"):
                path = args.output / name
                if path.exists():
                    record[name] = dict(sha256=sha(path), text=path.read_text(errors="replace"))
            json.dump(record, receipt, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(dict(passed=True, artifact=record["artifact"])), flush=True)

# AGENTS.md — tmm

## Overview
TMM (Traffic Management Microkernel) is F5's software data-plane engine for the modular BIG-IP (mBIP) platform. It processes network traffic at high speed — handling L4–L7 protocols, SSL, DNS, policy enforcement, NAT, and more — and is deployed as a containerized service within the Kubernetes-based SPK/mBIP stack. Control-plane configuration is delivered via MCP and PBUF message handlers; the resulting runtime state drives the fast-path packet processing pipeline.

## Quick Reference
- **Language(s)**: C (primary, ~95%), Python (test tooling/scripts, ~4%), Bash (~1%)
- **Build System**: GNU Make + Docker toolchain container (`make start` → `make tmm`)
- **Runtime Environment**: Ubuntu 24.04-based container (`f5-runtime-base-ubuntu24-04`), deployed on Kubernetes (SPK/mBIP)
- **Test Framework**: Custom C unit test runner (`test/unit/obj_x86_64.gcovut/t`), pytest + Tao for SSA functional tests, Robot Framework for access tests

## Critical Constraints
These are things an AI MUST know to avoid generating broken code:

1. **TMM CANNOT be compiled outside the build container.** Always use `make tmm` (or `make debug`) from the repo root — this delegates to the Docker toolchain. Running `make -C src/compile` directly only works from inside the container (`make interactive`). Never suggest bare compiler invocations outside this context.

2. **TMM cannot be run directly — only via unit tests or SSA functional tests.** TMM requires `mapres` to map hugepages and set up hardware-accelerated networking. Do not attempt to run or configure the `tmm` or `mapres` binaries. Use `make unittest` or `make -C test/ssa_functional run` to exercise code.

3. **All type primitives must come from `src/sys/types.h`.** Use `UINT8`, `UINT32`, `UINT64`, `BOOL`, `INT32`, etc. — never use raw C types like `unsigned int` directly where these apply. The file also redefines `double` and `float` to struct wrappers (`__double`, `__float`) to prevent accidental floating-point use in the data path; do not `#include` system headers that conflict with this.

4. **All source files must be registered in `src/compile/filelist` (or a per-module `filelist.mk`).** The build system does not auto-discover `.c` files — a new file that is not added to the filelist will be silently excluded from the build.

5. **Functions must have a single return point; use `goto out` for early exits.** The exit label must be named `out`. This is a hard style requirement enforced by code review and the automated `clang-style-check` CI job.

6. **Build output must be verified by checking the artifact timestamp.** Do not treat a successful `make` exit as proof of a working build. The build is only successful when `src/compile/obj_x86_64.<debug|no_pgo>/tmm.{debug|no_pgo}` exists with an up-to-date modification time. Important errors appear at the **end** of build output — never `head` it.

7. **The TMM is OS-independent by design.** Do not `#include` system headers or introduce new library dependencies without explicit approval. Use the shim layer in `src/kern/` to access OS facilities. Do not replicate libc or syscall declarations in your own code.

8. **Run [pylint](https://pypi.org/project/pylint/) and [black](https://pypi.org/project/black/) against all generated _ssa-functional-tests_**.  Accept all recommended code changes.

9. **Initialize all variables declared on the stack in the unit test code.**  The unit test code is not performance critical but it is fragile and sensitive to minor changes in memory usage.

## Anti-Patterns — What NOT to Do

- **Do not use `L7_POLICY_ACTION_RESET`** — this action is deprecated (see `src/base/policy_bind.c:2791`). Use `shutdown+connection` instead.

- **Do not call `pool_add()` for next-hop routing entries** — in `src/mcp/db_route.c`, next-hop pools must be managed via `nh_pools` directly. The comment at line 250 explicitly forbids `pool_add` in that context.

- **Do not use `sa_trans_from_cookie_complete_deprecated()`** — this function in `src/base/sa_trans.c` is explicitly named deprecated and must not be called in new code. Use the non-deprecated `sa_trans_from_cookie_complete()` variant.

- **Do not use `//` single-line comments** — TMM uses `/* */` block comment style exclusively throughout all C source files.

- **Do not use `double` or `float` literals/variables directly** — `src/sys/types.h` redefines them to opaque struct wrappers. Use `DOUBLE` or `FLOAT` typedefs, or restructure to avoid floating-point entirely in data-path code.

- Use **BSD style** for C code.

- Keep lines **under 76 columns**.

- Use **4 spaces** for indentation, and **no tabs**.
  - Indent wrapped lines by two indents (8 spaces)

- When modifying code, **keep the style consistent with the existing code**.

- In conditional statements, use a parenthesis for non-trivial sub-clauses: ((a != NULL) || ready())

- **Do not hardcode version numbers in `docker_build/modules-libs.json.template`** — version strings must be sourced from `input-manifest.yml` via gomplate templating. Hardcoded versions break the stagebot automated update process.

## Key Entry Points

- **MCP control-plane message handlers**: `src/mcp/` — each `db_*.c` file handles a specific configuration object type (e.g., `db_net.c` for network interfaces, `db_route.c` for routing, `db_profile.c` for profiles)
- **PBUF declarative handlers**: `src/pbuf/` — handles the declarative configuration API layer
- **HUD filter pipeline**: `src/modules/hudfilter/` — all HUD (data-path) filter implementations; filters are chained via `src/modules/hudchain.c`
- **Plugin manager**: `src/modules/plugin_manager.c` — registers and drives all loadable modules/plugins
- **Type system**: `src/sys/types.h` — fundamental typedefs used across the entire codebase
- **Build registration**: `src/compile/filelist` (and per-module `filelist.mk`) — every `.c` file must be listed here
